items.name: The winter ferry: five sailings a day from 5 October
items.teaser: Since 5 October the Geyikli boat runs five times a day, four on weekdays; the late boats only Friday to Sunday
items.story: The hourly summer boat is over. A ferry-information site that follows GESTAŞ reports that the winter timetable on the Geyikli–Bozcaada line began on 5 October 2026: five sailings a day, four on weekdays, with three to four hours between them. Boats leave Geyikli at 08:00, 11:00, 15:00, 19:00 and 23:00, and Bozcaada at 07:00, 10:00, 14:00, 18:00 and 22:00; the two late sailings run only on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Earlier, on 14 September, the hourly service had already dropped to every two hours. In a hard north wind sailings are cancelled outright.
items.why: Plan the last boat back before you plan dinner, and on a weekday the last one leaves the island at 18:00.
facts: Fare not confirmed for winter 2026; check GESTAŞ

items.name: A late swim: the sea about 20 °C in October
items.teaser: October water averages about 20 °C off the island, by the climate tables, and November drops to about 18 °C
items.story: The air turns first; the sea holds on. Climate tables for Bozcaada give an October average of about 20 °C, with a range from 16 to 24 °C across the month; a second set gives 19.8 °C for October and about 18 °C for November. That is the north Aegean, cooler than the Turkish south coast at the same date. The rule of the island still holds: on a north poyraz swim the south sand at Ayazma, Sulubahçe or Habbele; when the lodos turns, cross to the east coves. In late October the loungers and beach cafés are gone, so bring everything.
items.why: Habbele, the bowl-shaped bay closest to town, is the calmest water on a windy day.
facts: Late Oct to mid-Nov, on a still, sunny day

items.story: This year the island's harvest festival ran from 14 to 23 August, earlier than the first week of September the old guides give, with a best-grape competition on the opening night. What the 2026 vintage is like, nobody has yet said in print: no figures for yield, start date or quality from the island's wineries or the Çanakkale agriculture office turned up in a search on 27 October. items.teaser: Family-run since 1948, Talay pours its own bottles from a shop in town; check it is open before you walk over
items.story: Talay is the island's oldest family winery still in the same hands: the brand was started in 1948 by the Talay brothers, Necati and Hayati, with a third brother, Sebati, named in one account, and bottled production began in 1955. It works the island grapes in a plain working-cellar key and pours at a tasting counter on Çınar Çeşme Sokağı in town, rather than from a visitors' tasting room. In winter the island empties and most places shorten their hours or shut; no November 2026 hours were found for the shop. Corvus, out by the vines, keeps limited visiting days even in season.

items.name: Palamut from the Strait: 125 to 150 lira a fish
items.teaser: Çanakkale's fish stalls report a plentiful palamut year; the first fish sold at 150 lira each in September
items.story: The fishing season in the Dardanelles opened on 1 September 2026, after the spring ban that began on 15 April. Çanakkale's first palamut, the Atlantic bonito that runs through the Strait in autumn, sold at 150 lira a fish; a later report has them at 125 to 150 lira as they grew larger, from 100 lira before. A stallholder, Engin Tunç, called it a year of plenty after poor seasons. Fishers working the Strait say the migration runs from September to December. For lüfer, the bluefish, no 2026 report was found; in October 2025 a fisherman out for lüfer brought back palamut.
items.why: Ask for palamut on the grill, or salted as lakerda, where a kitchen is still open.

Across the Edremit gulf, Ayvalık opened its new olive season with a ceremony in Altınova, and the first olives went straight to the press; the report's photograph is dated 2 October 2026. The head of the Ayvalık chamber of commerce, Ali Uçar, said yields in the region were high this season. items.name: The island kitchens go dark
items.teaser: Few places and hotels stay open in winter; the island fills briefly again at New Year
items.story: This is not a year-round island. The old guide counts almost three-quarters of the registered population leaving for the winter, and a national news report says very few venues and hotels stay open between autumn and spring, with some reopening for the New Year crowd. No list of which Bozcaada restaurants close, or on what date, was published for 2026, and none of the kept tables has posted its winter hours. In late October treat every meal as a phone call first. The Wednesday market in the castle square is a market for islanders, the ones who stay.

items.name: 29 October, Republic Day
items.teaser: Thursday 29 October is Republic Day, a national holiday; the afternoon of the 28th is a half day for offices
items.story: Türkiye was proclaimed a republic on 29 October 1923, the same year the Treaty of Lausanne left Bozcaada and Gökçeada to the new state. The day is a national public holiday; in 2026 it falls on a Thursday, and the afternoon of Wednesday 28 October is a half day for public offices. The island's main square, Cumhuriyet Meydanı, takes its name from the Republic, but no programme for the island's ceremonies was found. Banks and public offices close; the ferry keeps its winter timetable, and the late boats run only from Friday to Sunday.
items.why: On a Thursday holiday the late ferry does not run: the last boat off the island is at 18:00.

On 10 November the country stops at 09:05 to mark the hour of Atatürk's death in 1938, sirens and all. The next fixed date on the island is New Year, when a few hotels and kitchens open again for visitors. November is for the cellars, the palamut and an empty harbour.

items.name: Orthodox Easter, 2 May 2027
items.teaser: The island's few Orthodox families keep Easter; Orthodox Easter 2027 falls on Sunday 2 May
items.story: Bozcaada's Greek Orthodox community is down to a few dozen at most, but it keeps the feasts. News reports from past years describe an Easter service held at the island's Aya Yorgi chapel. The main church, Kimisis Theotokou in the Rum quarter, built in 1869, reopened for worship after a two-year restoration, with Patriarch Bartholomew leading the opening service. In 2027 Orthodox Easter falls on Sunday 2 May. Whether and where a service is held next spring has not been announced, and Hıdrellez, on 6 May, has no island event in any source we found.
items.why: Stand at the back, ask before you photograph, and leave a candle.

items.name: Aya Paraskevi at the Ayazma monastery, 26 July
items.teaser: Once a year, on 26 July, the shuttered monastery above Ayazma beach opens for its saint's day
items.story: The small monastery under the plane trees behind Ayazma beach is shut almost all year. On 26 July, the feast of Aya Paraskevi, it opens: Greek families from the island and from abroad come back for the service at the twin-spouted holy spring that gives the beach its name. In 2025 Patriarch Bartholomew presided, with the Greek Consul General in Istanbul and the PASOK leader Nikos Androulakis among those present; in 2019 the Metropolitan of Gökçeada and Bozcaada led it. In 2027 the date falls on a Monday. The festival around it is known on the island as the Ayazma fair.
items.why: Come early in the day; the lane to the monastery fills with cars by the service.
facts: The only day the monastery opens for worship; respect the service

items.story: The municipality's Kültür, Sanat ve Bağbozumu Festivali ran for ten days in 2026, from 14 to 23 August. It opened with a procession at 19:00 from the Jandarma fountain to Cumhuriyet Meydanı, the best-grape competition and a free concert at 21:30. Later days brought a talk on prehistoric grapes and wine, a Çavuş grape jam workshop, a grape-dish contest and, on 22 August, the launch of a Troya vine route. The 2026 edition was billed as the 26th, which, if held every year, puts the first near 2001; the old guide says both 'since 1999' and 'since the mid-1990s'.

items.name: 15 August, the Dormition
items.teaser: The church of St Mary is the church of the Dormition; its feast is 15 August, after a fortnight's fast
items.story: The church in the Rum quarter, Kimisis Theotokou, built in 1869 with a bell tower of 1895, is dedicated to the Dormition, the falling asleep of the Virgin. The feast has been kept on 15 August since the reign of the emperor Maurice, at the end of the sixth century, and Orthodox churches across Türkiye keep it after a fast from 1 to 15 August. On neighbouring Gökçeada it is the summer's great homecoming. For Bozcaada we found no report of the 2026 service and no schedule for 2027, which falls on a Sunday.
items.why: Ask in the Rum quarter whether a liturgy is planned before you count on one.
facts: 15 Aug each year (Sun 15 Aug 2027); service unconfirmed

bougie.title: 1925 — A Greek cellar becomes the first Turkish winery
bougie.desc: How Tenedos wine passed from the island's Greek growers to Turkish families, through the state monopoly years, to the 2002 revival.
bougie.lede: Tenedos stamped grapes on its money more than two thousand years ago, and for most of the centuries since the island's wine was made by its Greek families. In 1925 a Turkish family bought a Greek's workshop and began making it themselves. What followed was monopoly, decline and, from 2002, a revival on the island's own grapes.
paras: Silver coins struck on Tenedos in about 375 to 350 BC already pair a double-headed axe with a bunch of grapes, and the island's mint was still using the two together around 100 to 70 BC. Island tradition says Tenes, who gave Tenedos its name, found a wild vine near today's Poyraz Limanı and bred Kuntra from it: a legend, not a record. Local accounts also claim the island exported some 800,000 barrels of wine a year in the mid-1800s; we found no independent source for the figure.

By the island's own accounts, Turkish farmers grew grapes and sold them to the Greek families who made the wine until 1925. Lausanne in 1923 kept the island with Türkiye and its Greeks from the exchange (see 'Left out of the exchange'), but the community left over the decades and took its skills with it. In 1925 the Yunatçılar family, later Çamlıbağ, bought a workshop from a Greek as the island's first Turkish Muslim winemaker; Ataol reportedly dates from 1927, and the Talay brothers started their brand in 1948.

The state built its winery at Tekirdağ in 1925, and for much of the century Tekel, the alcohol and tobacco monopoly, dominated the trade; its wine side was sold in 2004. Island accounts date machine production to 1956, call 1960 to 1980 the peak and record a decline after it, with vineyards being torn up. In 2002 the architect Reşit Soley founded Corvus on the island, first harvest 2004 by one account. Six wineries now work Çavuş, Vasilaki, Karalahna and Kuntra.
